blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, a pattern switch over a Temporal value has a case for LocalDate, one for LocalTime and one for Instant. What else must it have to compile?

options.text: Nothing more, since the java.time interfaces are sealed
options.says: The page says the temporal interfaces are not sealed, so these cases alone do not cover every possible value.

options.text: A default branch, since the java.time interfaces are open
options.says: The page says the temporal interfaces are not sealed, so such a switch needs a default branch.

options.text: A null case, since the java.time interfaces are open
options.says: The page names a default branch as what such a switch needs; a null case does not cover the other types.

questions.stem: Per this page, which type should an audit log use to record the moment each event happened?

options.text: LocalTime, the type the page gives for alarms
options.says: The page gives LocalTime for opening hours and alarms, a time of day with no date, not for timestamps.

options.text: LocalDate, the type the page gives for holidays
options.says: The page gives LocalDate for birthdays and holidays, dates with no time, not for timestamps.

options.text: Instant, the type the page gives for machine time
options.says: The page lists Instant for timestamps and machine time, and says to store timestamps as Instant.

concepts: The temporal interfaces are not sealed, so a pattern switch over the concrete java.time types needs a default branch.
Instant fits timestamps, LocalDate birthdays and holidays, LocalTime opening hours and ZonedDateTime cross-zone scheduling.
